original_question: Let n be a positive integer. For a finite group K and an automorphism n−1 ϕ of K of order dividing n, let Xn,ϕ (K):= {x ∈ K | xxϕ · · · xϕ = 1}. Let cn be the supremum of the ratios |Xn,ϕ (H)|/|H| over all finite groups H and their automorphisms ϕ ∈ Aut(H) such that ϕn = id and Xn,ϕ (H) ̸= H. (a) Let n > 1 be a positive integer such that cd < 1 for all prime power divisors d of n. Is it true that cn < 1? (b) For a finite group G and a positive integer n, the generalized Hughes–Thompson subgroup is defined as Hn(G) = ⟨x ∈ G | xn ̸= 1⟩. Suppose that n is a positive integer for which there is a positive integer kn depending only on n such that |G: Hn(G)| ⩽ kn for all finite groups G with Hn(G) ̸= 1. Is it true that then cn < 1? This question is open even when n ⩾ 5 is prime.
target_in_paper: The draft does not correspond verbatim to a statement in arXiv:1401.0300. In that arXiv paper, the nearest official source item is Problem 14.53 (the Levai-Pyber conjecture on profinite groups with many solutions of x^n = 1). The draft itself matches, almost word for word, the later follow-up Questions 1.5 and 1.6 in Section 1 of Abdollahi-Malekan, which are posed in the context of Conjectures 1.1-1.3 and Proposition 1.4.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right group-theoretic objects from the later reformulation: the set X_{n,phi}(K), the constant c_n defined as a supremum over finite groups and automorphisms with phi^n = id, the generalized Hughes-Thompson subgroup H_n(G) = < x in G | x^n != 1 >, and the two specific open implications asking whether certain hypotheses force c_n < 1. It also correctly reflects the surrounding motivation from the bounded-index problem for Hughes-Thompson subgroups.
missing_details: It is not paper-faithful to arXiv:1401.0300 as stated: the closest official item there is Problem 14.53, whereas your c_n/H_n formulation comes from a later paper built around that Kourovka problem.
The definition of X_{n,phi}(K) should explicitly read x x^phi x^{phi^2} ... x^{phi^{n-1}} = 1; the draft has a typographical compression of the iterates of phi.
The supremum defining c_n should be stated cleanly as ranging over all finite groups H and phi in Aut(H) with phi^n = id and X_{n,phi}(H) != H.
The later paper states the prime case in Question 1.5 as open even when n > 5 is prime, not n >= 5.
Since the source has two separate questions, the stand-alone version should either keep them as two labeled parts or explicitly ask whether either hypothesis is sufficient to imply c_n < 1.

No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are purely group-theoretic (finite groups for c_n and H_n, profinite groups only in the motivating Kourovka problem).
refined_question:
Let n be a positive integer. For a group K and an automorphism phi in Aut(K) with phi^n = id, define X_{n,phi}(K) = { x in K | x x^phi x^{phi^2} ... x^{phi^{n-1}} = 1 }. Define
c_n = sup { |X_{n,phi}(H)| / |H| : H is a finite group, phi in Aut(H), phi^n = id, and X_{n,phi}(H) != H }.
For a finite group G, let H_n(G) = < x in G | x^n != 1 >.
Question: (a) If n > 1 and c_d < 1 for every prime-power divisor d of n, must c_n < 1? (b) If there exists an integer k_n depending only on n such that |G : H_n(G)| <= k_n for every finite group G with H_n(G) != 1, must c_n < 1? (For part (b), this is open even when n > 5 is prime.)
justification: The Kourovka Notebook item in arXiv:1401.0300 is Problem 14.53, a profinite-group conjecture about positive Haar measure of the solution set of x^n = 1. Your draft, however, does not ask that profinite/Haar-measure question directly; instead it uses the finite-group reformulation via the constants c_n and the generalized Hughes-Thompson subgroup H_n(G). Those notions, together with the two exact open questions you wrote, appear in Section 1 of Abdollahi-Malekan as Questions 1.5 and 1.6, after Conjectures 1.1-1.3 and Proposition 1.4 set up the notation and motivation. The rewrite therefore preserves your intended c_n/H_n formulation, fixes the exact iterated-automorphism product in X_{n,phi}(K), restores the precise quantifiers, and corrects the later paper's wording that the prime case remains open for n > 5. If one were to stay strictly inside arXiv:1401.0300, the official target would instead be Problem 14.53, which is broader than your draft and therefore not the closest narrow match.
